claims.claim: R1 beats OpenAI o1 on AIME (79.8 vs 79.2), MATH-500 (97.3 vs 96.4) and SWE-bench Verified (49.2 vs 48.9)
R1 is available on Hugging Face under an MIT license, usable commercially without restrictions
R1 contains 671 billion parameters (37B activated, MoE)
Distilled versions from 1.5B to 70B were released alongside the full model
API priced 90-95% cheaper than o1 ($0.55/$2.19 per 1M tokens vs o1's $15/$60)

delta: First downloadable open-weight (MIT) model at frontier reasoning level; the comparable model (o1) is API-only and closed
R1-Zero shows reasoning behaviour emerging from pure RL with no supervised fine-tuning first, validated in the open
Six distilled checkpoints (1.5B-70B) shipped the same day, putting strong reasoning on local hardware

prior_art.differs: Comparable reasoning performance but closed weights, API-only, ~27x the API price; R1 ships downloadable MIT weights plus distills
prior_art.name: OpenAI o1

prior_art.differs: Open reasoning model from Nov 2024, but well below o1 level (AIME 44.0 in DeepSeek's comparison table) and a preview release; R1 is a full release at o1 level
prior_art.name: QwQ-32B-Preview (Alibaba)

category_record.license: MIT (weights and code; distillation explicitly permitted)

recheck_when: When independent benchmark replication lands (third-party evals, arena-style rankings)
tldr: An open-weights (MIT) 671B reasoning model matching o1 on its maker's own benchmarks, downloadable on day one with laptop-sized distills - the benchmark numbers just aren't independently verified yet.
